title: Extrema on a Circle: Sweep the Boundary
topic: Maximise and minimise f(x, y) = x² + 2y² on the unit circle by parametrising the boundary as (cos θ, sin θ). Then g(θ) = 1 + sin²θ traces a one-variable curve whose peaks and troughs are the constrained max (0, ±1) and min (±1, 0). At each extreme the level curve of f is tangent to the circle and ∇f points along the radius — the Lagrange condition.

beats.narration: How large can a function get if you are trapped on a circle?

elements.content: Stuck on a circle — where is f biggest?

beats.narration: The function f equals x squared plus two y squared grows without bound in the plane. But restrict it to the unit circle, and there is a largest value and a smallest value.

beats.narration: Walk around the circle with the angle theta. The value rises to its maximum at the top and bottom, and falls to its minimum at the left and right, tracing a smooth curve below.

beats.narration: At each extreme, the level curve of f just grazes the circle — the gradient of f points straight along the radius. That is exactly the Lagrange condition.

beats.narration: To optimise on a boundary, parametrise it and turn a two variable problem into a single one.
